findings.title: Empty authored fake falls through to the live provider adapter
findings.problem: The reachability check records service names even when a fake has zero outcomes. The parser and fixture validator accept that empty block. Lowering only creates entries while visiting outcomes, so an empty block emits no fake for ReminderMail.send_overdue_reminder. The generated operation lookup returns null, selecting oneAttempt and live Bun.connect.
findings.trigger: Remove only the accepted outcome from fixture service_accepted in canonical fixture 170, retaining service ReminderMail: fake {} and its secret fixture configuration.
findings.impact: An otherwise checked authored test can attempt external side effects and send its fixture bearer key if connections are not blocked, violating RM-304's zero-real-side-effects acceptance. Normal canonical tests do not cover empty fake blocks.
findings.requiredChange: Reject an empty fake for a reachable operation, or emit an explicit empty operation sequence whose exhaustion is OutcomeUnknown. Generated authored test invocation must fail closed if its fake mapping is missing instead of selecting production transport.
findings.requiredRegression: Compile/run an authored empty fake with both Bun.connect and fetch blocked; expect static rejection or a contained no-network fake outcome.

findings.title: Earlier fake operations exhaust the deadline of a fresh callable operation
findings.problem: Each authored call captures a fresh logical operation with a fresh monotonic start and attempt budget, while sharing the per-test fake sequence and cumulative elapsedMs. invokeReferenceMail computes its current time as the NEW context start plus ALL earlier fake elapsed time, but its deadline as only the new start plus 30 seconds. Earlier independent operations are therefore charged against the new operation.
findings.trigger: One fixture sequence contains six pre_dispatch_timeout outcomes followed by acceptance. In a single authored test, call classify_delivery three times. Each top-level call is a separate operation.
findings.expected: The third new operation consumes the queued acceptance using its fresh three-attempt/30-second allowance. The second operation's third timeout should not be shortened by time charged to the first operation.
findings.requiredChange: Keep the fixture sequence cursor shared, but measure fake elapsed time against a logical-operation baseline. Nested calls in the SAME operation must retain their shared attempt/deadline budget, and independent authored calls must begin with a fresh relative deadline.
findings.requiredRegression: Exercise three sequential top-level callable operations on one fixture plus a nested-call case, asserting the cursor, attempts, timeout durations and accepted third receipt.

observations.result: The exported host fake seam accepts accepted_at:'not-an-instant' and a valid accepted_at with extra object keys as accepted; it only checks typeof accepted_at. An empty value maps to OutcomeUnknown. This is narrower validation than real HTTP classifyResponse.
observations.scopeLimit: No malformed authored-receipt exploit is established: source fixtures require a direct declared output construction, typed fields, and generated Instant/output validation. The reviewed canonical fake supplies canonical checked data. Treat the direct host seam's loose validation as a limitation of malformed-response evidence; it is not an additional blocking public-language finding.
observations.suggestion: If host-level malformed fake values are intended as supported probes, use the same closed receipt validator and OutcomeUnknown classification rather than relying only on a numeric accepted_at test.

acceptanceEvidence.result: Canonical fixture checks; unknown operation/outcome, duplicate fake and absent fake fail with stable rules. Public fake AST offers accepted constructions or declared outcome names, not host callbacks.

acceptanceEvidence.area: Request and response typing, secret sinks
acceptanceEvidence.result: Wrong callable request and accepted response construction are rejected. config.mail_api_key cannot be read in the response construction environment. Generated service wrapper validates ReminderMessage before invokeReferenceMail and validates ReminderReceipt before returning it. HTTP receipt checks remain in classifyResponse; host fake seam limit is recorded above.

Generated per-test allocation resets cursor/elapsed state; the registered suite runs six authored tests twice with the expected retry/outcome sequence, including separate tests sharing service_retry. Independent-operation elapsed accounting within a test fails finding RM304-FRESH-OPERATION-DEADLINE.

Registered tests pass known-no-effect timeout retries, rate-limit retry, malformed acknowledgement and possible-dispatch timeout without blind retry, numeric malformed receipt, exhaustion, and route deadline cap. Unknown leaves the later accepted outcome unconsumed.

Registered attempt-log canary assertions pass. Both generated authored probe reports and captured logs contain no fixture secret canary. Attempt logs retain only operation/attempt/time/outcome/retry fields. No runtime HTTP credential leak was tested or claimed.

Canonical tests make zero provider connections; readiness blocks both connection and fetch paths. Empty checked fake attempts three blocked provider connections, so universal zero-effects acceptance fails. Probes never permitted a real network call.
